messages.subject: reactiveValues in global.R
parts:
Hi all. I commented a while back about defining reactiveValues() objects in the global.R file. I hadn't figured that this would be desired, but was informed that it is like that by design, and the expectation is for users to be able to modify some global data structure... presumably, triggering reactive elements across all users using the app at that time.

Can anyone point me to a shiny application that does a good job of demonstrating how this sort of global reactivity might be put to good use?

Thank you,
Dan

messages.author: a58a2a3609db3342
messages.subject: Re: reactiveValues in global.R
parts:
It was designed this way so shiny app users could communicate across time and space. Badly written example here http://spark.rstudio.com/johnharrison/rChat/.

global.R
---------------------
globReact <- reactiveValues(chatDF =
                              data.frame(username = c(''), msgdt = c("A long time ago"), msg = c("Welcome to rChat")
                                         , stringsAsFactors = FALSE))

ui.R
--------------------
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
 
  headerPanel("RChat"),
  sidebarPanel(
    textInput("user", "Preferred Username:", paste0("Luke", sample(1:100, 1)))
    , textInput("msg", "Submit a message")
    , tags$div(actionButton("submit", "Submit", icon("refresh")))
  )
    ,
  mainPanel(
    dataTableOutput("chatLog")
  )
))

server.R
-------------------
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  output$chatLog <- renderDataTable({
    globReact$chatDF
  })
 
  observe({
    x <- as.numeric(input$submit)
    if(x > 0){
      isolate(globReact$chatDF <- rbind(globReact$chatDF, c(username = input$user, msgdt = as.character(Sys.time()), msg = input$msg)))
    }
    updateTextInput(session, "msg", value = "")
  }
  )
 
})
